haiku-low.q1: Three consecutive breaching evaluations (rate above 2%, at least 500 requests), and no unresolved incident already exists for that service and rule.
haiku-low.q2: The breach is recorded on the existing incident, no new actions are created, and nobody is paged.
haiku-low.q3: Ten consecutive minutes below 1% resolve it. A later breach finds no unresolved incident and opens a new one.
haiku-low.q4: Level 1 (primary) immediately at opening, level 2 (secondary) at +5 minutes, level 3 (EM) at +10 minutes, unless acknowledged or resolved first.
haiku-low.q5: Send SMS instead. If SMS also fails, log it in page_log and move on; no retry, and the next level fires on schedule.
haiku-low.q6: Only people already paged, the distinct people in page_log, get a resolved notice. Pending page actions are cancelled.
haiku-low.q7: In Postgres evaluations table, one row per service, rule and minute. Streaks read from latest rows; a missing minute breaks the streak.
haiku-low.q8: A unique key on evaluations (service, rule, minute) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and a partial unique index refusing a second unresolved incident.
haiku-low.q9: A page action's due_at time triggers it. The worker cancels it if acknowledged or resolved, otherwise looks up the on-call person and sends the page.
haiku-low.q10: The provider's webhook, carrying the incident id, reaches either instance. One transaction sets acked_by and acked_at and cancels pending page actions.
haiku-low.q11: When each level fires, the schedule service is queried for who is on call then, not when the incident opens.
haiku-low.q12: From page_log, which records every send attempt; its distinct people are the recipients of the resolved notice actions.

sonnet.q1: The last 3 consecutive minutes' evaluations are all breaching (rate above 2% with at least 500 requests), and there is no unresolved incident for that (service, rule).
sonnet.q2: The breach is recorded on the existing incident; no new incident, no actions are created, and nobody is paged (partial unique index rejects a second unresolved incident).
sonnet.q3: The last 10 consecutive evaluations are all below 1% and the incident is unresolved: resolved_at is set, pending page actions are cancelled, and resolved notices are queued for people in page_log. A later breach finds no unresolved incident and opens a new one.
sonnet.q4: Level 1 (primary) due when the incident opens, level 2 (secondary) at +5 minutes, level 3 (EM) at +10 minutes, unless acknowledged or resolved before then.
sonnet.q5: Push failure falls back to SMS. If SMS also fails, it is logged in page_log and the worker moves on; no retry, and the next level still fires on schedule. Level 3 failure should trigger an alert. Schedule lookup failure is retried a few times within seconds, then logged and moved on.
sonnet.q6: One resolved notice per distinct person in page_log (people already paged) is sent by push, falling back to SMS, with a few retries. Pending page actions are cancelled in the same transaction that sets resolved_at.
sonnet.q7: In the Postgres evaluations table (one row per service, rule, minute); the streak is read from the latest 3 or 10 rows. A missing minute (e.g. failed metrics query) breaks the streak; for breaches, a non-breaching evaluation also breaks it.
sonnet.q8: They don't talk to each other. A unique key on evaluations (service, rule, minute) with INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means only the first insert succeeds and the other stops. A partial unique index on incidents (service, rule) where resolved_at IS NULL prevents a second unresolved incident.
sonnet.q9: Each action row's due_at; workers poll Postgres every few seconds, claim a due action with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and lock the incident row. If the incident is acknowledged or resolved the action is marked cancelled; otherwise it looks up the on-call person and sends the page.
sonnet.q10: The engineer taps Acknowledge at the paging provider, which calls the webhook (carrying the incident id) on either instance's worker. It locks the incident row, then in one transaction sets acked_by and acked_at and cancels pending page actions. An already-claimed action waits for the incident lock, sees the ack and cancels itself.
sonnet.q11: When each level fires (when the action is processed), by asking the schedule service who is on call right now, not when the incident opens.
sonnet.q12: At resolution, one resolved-notice action is added per distinct person in the page_log table; the worker claims those actions and sends them.
